prompt: In two or three sentences of plain prose, explain why adding an index to a database table can make writes slower. No bullet points, no headings, no code.
why: STE sentence-length and plain-word rules: length limits, and English instead of Latin abbreviations or inflated verbs. A short explanatory answer is where an unconstrained model reaches for 'i.e.' and 'leverage' most readily. Note the gap between rule and grader: the skill states 25 words, but this grader fails only above 35. Measured, the model does not hold 25 on an explanation carrying a three-item list ('When you insert, update, or delete a row in a table, the database must also update every index on that table' is 28 words and hard to shorten without losing content). A check that can never pass stops being run, so the grader is a ceiling on runaway sentences rather than a restatement of the target: it still catches the 39-word case this prompt produced before, while 25 stays the number to aim at.
